name: Nongkhnum River Island
description: Largest river island in Meghalaya, formed by the bifurcation of the Kynshi River into Phanliang and Namliang. Features sandy beaches, clear streams, grasslands, and nearby waterfalls. About 14 km from Nongstoin; often called Asia's second-largest river island (though the claim is exaggerated).
facts: Area approximately 21 km²
About 14 km from Nongstoin, West Khasi Hills HQ
Access via bridge over Weinia Falls or ferry in some seasons
Low tourist infrastructure, ideal for quiet nature visits

name: Langshiang Falls
description: Major plunge waterfall on the Kynshi River near Sangriang village, about 24 km from Nongstoin. Claimed height around 337 m (needs confirmation); offers panoramic views of green hills and can be viewed from Mawpon village. Also known as Kshaid Ur-Nar.
facts: Located near Sangriang village, 24 km from Nongstoin
Formed by Kynshi River after island split
Short trek from village; low crowds
One of the taller waterfalls in Meghalaya

name: Weinia Falls (Kshaid Weinia)
description: Powerful waterfall near Nongkhnum Island on the Kynshi River system, surrounded by dense forest and cliffs. Entry point to the island via bridge over the falls in some descriptions; popular with locals for picnics and fishing pools nearby.
facts: Near Nongkhnum River Island, West Khasi Hills
About 14-20 km from Nongstoin
Bridge over falls used to access island
Best after monsoon for full flow

name: Nongstoin Town
description: District headquarters of West Khasi Hills, a quiet hill town at about 1,400 m elevation. Serves as the main base for exploring Nongkhnum Island, nearby waterfalls, and Khasi cultural areas. Features local markets and is the administrative center for the district.
facts: Headquarters of West Khasi Hills district
Elevation around 1409 m
About 90-100 km from Shillong
Base for day trips to Nongkhnum and falls

name: Mawlangkhar Village
description: Peaceful offbeat village in West Khasi Hills near Nongstoin, surrounded by forests, streams, and scenic hills. Often compared to a mini Dzukou for its meadows and calm atmosphere; offers trails, traditional Khasi culture, and quiet nature experiences away from popular tourist circuits.
facts: About 12-14 km from Nongstoin
Referred to as Meghalaya's Dzukou Valley in local descriptions
Traditional Khasi matrilineal community
Ideal for slow, quiet nature stays

name: Mairang Town
description: District headquarters of Eastern West Khasi Hills, a quiet hill town at about 1,564 m elevation on the Shillong-Nongstoin road. Serves as the main gateway and base for exploring Kyllang Rock, Mawthadraishan Peak, nearby valleys, and Khasi cultural sites. Features local markets and administrative offices.
facts: Headquarters of Eastern West Khasi Hills district (created 2021)
Elevation around 1564 m
About 40-45 km from Shillong on NH-106
Base for day trips to Kyllang Rock and Mawthadraishan

name: Mawthadraishan Peak
description: Highest peak in Eastern West Khasi Hills at 1,924.5 m, located midway between Mairang and Nongstoin on the Mawthadraishan Range. Offers panoramic views of Assam plains, Garo Hills, Khasi Hills, and distant Himalayas on clear days. Features small natural ponds near the summit; popular for short treks and photography.
facts: Elevation 1924.5 m, highest in the district
Located approximately midway between Mairang and Nongstoin
Short trek from nearby villages like Mawroh or Nongshillong
Clear post-monsoon views of Himalayas possible

name: Kyllang Rock
description: Massive monolithic granite dome (locally Lum Kyllang) rising about 1,774 m near Mairang. Steeped in Khasi folklore as a figure who battled Symper Rock; climbable via a short trail with rest points for panoramic views of pine forests, valleys, and villages. Northern and eastern flanks accessible; southern side steep with detached blocks.
facts: About 10-13 km from Mairang, ~55-60 km from Shillong
Diameter ~300 m, elevation ~1774 m
Linked to Khasi legends of gods Kyllang and Symper
Short uphill trail from base; best October to April

name: Markham and Remkhla Valley
description: Scenic rolling hills and valleys (locally Laitmurok viewpoint) spanning Markham and Mawkyllei villages on the border area of Eastern West Khasi Hills and South West Khasi Hills. Known for misty mornings, green grasslands, grazing lands, and tranquil rural landscapes. Remkhla section features streams and hanging bridges.
facts: Located between Markham and Mawkyllei villages
About 25 km from Mairang
Features Wahrilang hanging bridges in Remkhla section
Emerging offbeat destination with low infrastructure

name: Ka Phan Nonglait Falls
description: Serene waterfall in lush forests of Eastern West Khasi Hills, named after an unsung warrior who fought the British. Surrounded by dense greenery, it offers a peaceful atmosphere for nature visits and short trails.
facts: Named after local warrior Phan Nonglait
Near Mairang area in Eastern West Khasi Hills
Surrounded by dense forest; low crowds
Official tourism-listed attraction

name: Tirot Sing Ecological Park
description: Recreational park in Mairangbah village featuring a colonial-era pine tree, statue of U Tirot Sing (Khasi freedom fighter), children's play area, and viewpoints for sunrise/sunset over Mairang Town. Combines history, nature, and local culture.
facts: Located in Mairangbah village near Mairang Town
Features U Tirot Sing statue and colonial pine tree
Play area and town views
Named after the Siem of Nongkhlaw who resisted British rule

name: Law Lyngdoh Nonglait Sacred Grove
description: Protected sacred forest (Law Kyntang) in the Nonglait/Lawbyrtun-Mawkyllei area of Eastern West Khasi Hills, managed by local clans. High biodiversity with rare flora; traditional taboos prohibit removal of anything from the grove. One of the larger groves in the region supporting streams and cultural rituals.
facts: Approximately 50 hectares, clan-managed
Located near Nonglait village, Mawthadraishan area
High species diversity; traditional protection by beliefs
Part of broader Law Lyngdoh sacred forest network

name: Mawkyrwat Town
description: District headquarters of South West Khasi Hills, a quiet hill town serving as the main gateway and base for exploring hot springs, caves, viewpoints, and border areas. Known for its local markets and Khasi cultural surroundings.
facts: Headquarters of South West Khasi Hills district (formed 2012 from West Khasi Hills)
About 75 km from Shillong
Elevation around 1360-1500 m
Base for day trips to Jakrem, Ranikor, and Nongnah

name: Jakrem Hot Spring
description: Natural sulphur hot spring near Lawblei (Jakrem) on the Shillong-Mawkyrwat road, about 15 km from Mawkyrwat. Believed to have medicinal properties; popular picnic and bathing spot especially in winter, with bathing compartments available.
facts: 15 km from Mawkyrwat, ~60-64 km from Shillong
Sulphur water believed to have curative properties
Favourite winter picnic and bathing spot
Official district places-of-interest listing

name: Symper Rock (Sympher Rock)
description: Unique geological rock formation about 50 km from Shillong on the Shillong-Mawkyrwat road. Offers views of the Mawkyrwat area and surroundings from the top; one of the distinctive formations in the region.
facts: About 50 km from Shillong on Shillong-Mawkyrwat road
Unique geological formation
Panoramic views of Mawkyrwat area
Official district places-of-interest

name: Umngi River
description: Longest river in the Mawkyrwat subdivision, originating near Sohiong and flowing to Umpung Lake. Favourite picnic spot about 18 km from Mawkyrwat, with a small river island used for activities like beach volleyball.
facts: 18 km from Mawkyrwat
Longest river in Mawkyrwat sub-division
Small river island for local activities
Flows to scenic Umpung Lake

name: Phlangja Ud Cave
description: Beautiful cave about 16 km from Mawkyrwat near Phlangja Ud, south of Rangmaw village. Features stalactites; above it is vast grassland offering views of Bangladesh plains. Cave length around 600 meters.
facts: 16 km from Mawkyrwat
Stalactites on ceiling
Grassland above with Bangladesh plains views
About 600 m in extent

name: Rilang Viewpoint (Mawranglang)
description: Scenic valley and viewpoint about 5 km from Mawkyrwat at Mawranglang on the Nongstoin-Mawkyrwat road. Meandering across the river; convenient picnic and angling spot with green landscapes.
facts: 5 km from Mawkyrwat at Mawranglang
On Nongstoin-Mawkyrwat road
Picnic and angling spot
Official district listing; also noted in tourism visits

name: Synrangbah Cave
description: Large open cave at Nonglang, about 3 km from Mawkyrwat. The Mawkyrwat-Photjaud road passes through it; serves as shelter for people and cattle during rain; home to bats of various sizes.
facts: About 3 km from Mawkyrwat at Nonglang
Road passes through the leveled cave
Shelter during storms; bat habitat
Official district places-of-interest

name: Dongnob Falls
description: Beautiful waterfall about 8 km from Mawkyrwat at Photjaud. Features a cave in the middle that creates striking natural beauty with sun ray reflections in winter.
facts: 8 km from Mawkyrwat at Photjaud
Cave in the middle of the falls
Notable in winter with light reflections
Official district listing

name: Iawpaw Plateau (Nongnah)
description: Scenic plateau and tableland about 30 km from Mawkyrwat, southwest of Nongnah. Offers bird’s-eye views of surrounding hills, valleys, Bangladesh plains, rivers, and distant Himalayas. Legendarily resembles a bed; hosts one of the longest caves in the Khasi Hills.
facts: 30 km from Mawkyrwat near Nongnah
Views of Bangladesh plains and Himalayas
Longest cave in Khasi Hills on the plateau
Appears like a bed from distance; official listing

name: Ranikor
description: Border town about 45 km from Mawkyrwat, formerly a winter resort of the Queen of Maharam. Near Bangladesh border on the riverbank; famous for angling Golden Mahseer, boat rowing, and the annual tourism festival. Features the Borba Singh (Jadugata) Bridge.
facts: 45 km from Mawkyrwat, near Bangladesh border
Best spot for Golden Mahseer angling
Borba Singh Bridge (claimed second longest suspension in India)
Annual tourism festival in February; former royal winter resort
